The smallest positive real number \(C\) is the operator norm (induced 2-norm) of the matrix \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 \end{pmatrix}\). This norm equals the square root of the largest eigenvalue of \(A^T A\).

First, compute \(A^T A\):
\[
A^T A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 6 \\ 6 & 13 \end{pmatrix}.
\]

Next, find the eigenvalues of \(A^T A\):
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix} 4-\lambda & 6 \\ 6 & 13-\lambda \end{pmatrix} = (4-\lambda)(13-\lambda) - 36 = \lambda^2 - 17\lambda + 16 = 0.
\]
The eigenvalues are \(\lambda = 1\) and \(\lambda = 16\). The largest eigenvalue is 16, so the operator norm is \(\sqrt{16} = 4\).

Thus, \(\|A\mathbf{v}\| \le 4\|\mathbf{v}\|\) for all \(\mathbf{v}\), and \(C = 4\) is the smallest such constant.

Answer: 4
